title: Answering the Call for a Standard Reliability Measure for Coding Data; original alpha computing note
claim: Reliability requires independently generated comparable data; alpha supports multiple raters, measurement levels and missing observations. The linked original computing note defines frequency-based ordinal distance and a worked missing-data example.
limitations: Missing-data support does not remove sampling bias. A coefficient is not validity. Different distance and degenerate-case conventions must be disclosed.
verified_detail: Computing note dated 2011-01-25, bibliography updated 2013-09-13; example nominal 0.743, ordinal 0.815, interval 0.849. R Journal table uses an alternative equidistant-rank ordinal convention.

title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
claim: Predictive accuracy and probability calibration differ; post-processing calibration is evaluated on classification models.
limitations: Temperature-scaling effectiveness on the studied classifiers does not establish calibration of verbal LLM confidence or video judges.

title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
claim: Selective prediction can trade coverage for risk by rejecting uncertain examples.
limitations: Theoretical or empirical guarantees require the paper's setup; no imported error guarantee for a new media-judging system.

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Testing Statistical Significance in Natural Language Processing
claim: Statistical test selection must match task, experimental design and metric; pairwise comparisons require appropriate dependence handling.
limitations: This NLP methodology paper is not a complete solution for crossed video-prompt-rater sampling or multiple comparisons.

title: A Statistical Framework for Ranking LLM-Based Chatbots
claim: Pairwise preference ranking can explicitly model ties and competitor covariance.
limitations: Ranking assumptions and chatbot data do not validate a video leaderboard; inability to judge is conceptually separate from a tie.

title: Search-Time Data Contamination
claim: Retrieval-enabled agents can encounter benchmark question-answer pairs at evaluation time, creating contamination independent of model training leakage.
limitations: Reported frequencies are benchmark-specific; study is about text benchmark retrieval, not measured contamination of this lab.

title: Calibrating LLM Judges for Human and AI Conversations
claim: A small anchor set and calibration function improve cross-judge scale comparability in conversational-success evaluation; pairwise judging remains sensitive to transcript length and position.
limitations: Conversation tasks, not generative-video evaluation; calibration does not remove all ranking or discrimination weaknesses.

title: The Geometry of LLM-as-Judge: Why Inter-LLM Consensus Is Not Human Alignment
claim: Inter-judge agreement can reflect shared bias; comparing judges and held-out humans against the same reference avoids a favorable comparison created by averaging human references.
limitations: Evidence from Indic benchmarks and text judgments; do not generalize effect sizes to video. Page reports EMNLP 2026 acceptance.
verified_detail: Current v2 reports 42 judges; search snippets still described v1 with 41 judges.

title: Bias and Uncertainty in LLM-as-a-Judge Estimation
claim: Bias-corrected model comparisons can fail when calibration is unstable across models; shared calibration can reverse comparison direction in the studied setting.
limitations: Analytical results, simulations and MMLU-Pro case study; not a video validation or universal recommendation for a particular correction estimator.

title: What's a minimum viable evaluation setup?
claim: Hamel Husain and Shreya Shankar recommend starting with direct error analysis on a small set of traces and a domain-expert quality owner.
limitations: Experienced practitioner guidance, not randomized evidence that one expert or 20-50 examples suffices for statistical reliability.

title: ITU-T P.910 (07/2026): Subjective video quality assessment methods for multimedia applications
claim: The official catalog lists P.910 (07/2026) as in force, approved 2026-07-29, superseding 10/2023. The older edition public summary describes non-interactive subjective multimedia assessment.
limitations: Current edition status verified, but its detailed clause changes were not inspected. No edition-specific conformance or custom generative-media rubric validation is claimed.
verified_detail: Independent agent fact-check identified the new edition; both official catalog records were reopened to confirm current and superseded status.

title: NIST AI 600-1: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile and AI RMF status
claim: Voluntary generative-AI risk-management companion to AI RMF 1.0; the current official RMF page reports that 1.0 is being revised.
limitations: Not product certification, not an exhaustive media-quality benchmark, and an announced revision is not a new released framework.

title: The TEVV-Athlon Framework for Evaluating AI Systems, NIST AI 200-2 initial public draft announcement
claim: An extensible test, evaluation, verification and validation framework is proposed for real-world AI outcomes, including multimodal and agentic systems; comment period closes 2026-10-06.
limitations: Draft as of cutoff; cite as a design input, not a finalized standard or conformance certification.

title: ISO AI management, risk and quality-model standards: public scope and status
claim: ISO/IEC 42001 specifies organization-level AI management-system requirements; related 23894 provides AI risk guidance and 25059 a quality model.
limitations: Only public scopes/status inspected, not a licensed clause-level audit. No organizational or product certification is claimed. ISO/IEC 25059:2023 catalog identifies an FDIS replacement under development.

title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
claim: Entities, activities, agents, qualified association, roles, plans and delegation provide interoperable provenance concepts.
limitations: Provenance describes origins and responsibility but does not prove claim truth; domain objectives, constraints and authority enforcement remain application responsibilities.

title: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
claim: Validates RDF data graphs against declared shapes and constraints.
limitations: Structural conformance cannot establish empirical truth, causal identification or authorization to execute an action.

title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Primer, Second Edition
claim: OWL expresses knowledge semantics with an open-world assumption, so missing facts need not be false.
limitations: Application validation and explicit evidence/unknown states remain necessary; ontology consistency is not world-model accuracy.

title: C2PA Content Credentials technical specification 2.4 and official explainer
claim: C2PA supports tamper-evident content provenance; the official explainer states provenance alone does not establish factual truth and metadata can be incomplete or removed.
limitations: Valid signature does not verify scene truth, model quality or completeness; absence is not a synthetic-media verdict. Do not infer every ingredient's content has been independently revalidated.
verified_detail: Official 2.4 specification section 5.3.1 dates release April 2026, contradicting a discovered secondary search snippet's September date.

title: Causal Inference: What If, author-hosted edition
claim: Identifying causal effects requires a well-defined causal question and assumptions beyond associations; consistency, exchangeability and positivity matter in the discussed identification setups.
limitations: A hypothesis graph is not proof of causal identification; this source does not show that rendered-video mechanisms can always be distinguished.

title: TIO-SHACL: Comprehensive SHACL validation for TMF Intent Ontologies
claim: Demonstrates validation shapes for a telecommunications intent ontology, including quantity constraints and relationships between expectations.
limitations: Domain-specific telecom work, with target:ISWC noted but no acceptance claim in the inspected record. Proposed transfer is a validation pattern, not proof for media intent.
